Subject: Re: Sudden p99 latency spikes across all regions - urgent

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed sustained queue growth on NovatoHealth dedicated pool starting 08:38 PDT. Queue length increased ~6x within 5 minutes.
- Concurrency cap was hit on several hosts (cap=160/session_group) leading to backpressure. When caps were hit, requests queued in the runtime and small customers’ requests were starved.
- We see an uptick in KV cache miss rate (~32% -> 67%) during the same window; likely cache churn from a burst pattern.
- Model OOM/fallbacks: negligible — no evidence of a model regression in logs.

Proposed immediate mitigations (low-risk first):
1) Temporarily increase concurrency cap for NovatoHealth dedicated pool from 160 to 260 (risk: higher token cost and transient CPU/GPU load).
2) Enable prefix/KV caching for hot prefixes used by Novato (applies to session tokens for checkout flow).
3) Temporarily route non-critical traffic to a smaller model variant (reduce per-token latency).

I’ve attached a reduced logfile snippet and p99 trace samples.

[Attachment: p99_logs.zip]

Will continue to dig into root cause and post a fuller RCA.

-David
David Kim

Subject: Re: Sudden p99 latency spikes across all regions - urgent

Triage + immediate runbook itemization:
- Action 1 (15m): Increase concurrency cap to 260 via infra console: set pool.config["novatohealth"].concurrency_cap=260. Monitor queue length and p99.
- Action 2 (10m): Flip on prefix caching: runtime.config.cache.prefix=true for account namespace. This should cut KV misses by ~40-60% for repeat checkout flows.
- Action 3 (30m): Roll a model-variant route: route profile "checkout" -> model-variant "tiny-latency-v2" for non-critical paths. This requires ~2-minute config push but avoids impacting top-level checkout path.
- Action 4 (60m): Pre-warm KV cache for top-20 prefixes using a small replay of recent traffic (safe, read-only).

Risks & notes: bumping concurrency will raise outbound token cost and can briefly increase load on the dedicated hosts; we should keep autoscaling thresholds conservative and watch GPU mem. If we see sustained high CPU/GPU, we can auto-scale temporary burst capacity.

I can run Actions 1 & 2 immediately if Rachel signs off.

-Karthik

Date: 2026-10-22T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: NovatoHealth incident follow-up & exec summary (p99 spike)

Executive summary (for leadership):
- Impact: NovatoHealth experienced a sustained p99 tail-latency increase beginning 2026-10-20 08:38 PDT, peaking at ~6.1s. Error rate rose to 4.8% during the peak window. Affected production checkout flows; ~12% of requests during the window saw >2s latency.
- Root cause (initial): A sudden burst pattern caused KV cache churn and pushed hosts to their configured concurrency caps in Novato’s dedicated pool, leading to queueing/backpressure and observed tail latency. No model regression detected.
- Mitigation performed: Karthik and David executed a temporary concurrency cap increase (160 -> 260) and enabled prefix caching and a limited model-variant route for non-critical paths. We pre-warmed top prefixes. These actions reduced p99 from ~6.1s to ~1.3s within 22 minutes of the first mitigation.
- Residual risk & next steps: We recommend a controlled capacity increase (reserved burst) for NovatoHealth while we optimize caching and work with Novato on smoothing burst traffic patterns. Engineering will finish a full RCA and propose configuration hardening (adaptive concurrency caps, smarter cache eviction, traffic shaping).
- Customer asks: Novato requested an ETA for permanent fixes and an initial credit estimate for the SLA window.

Requested approvals:
- Marcus: authorize up to two weeks of temporary reserved burst capacity for NovatoHealth (estimate: $12k/week) while RCA and tuning are completed.
- Finance/Procurement: approve pro-rated billing adjustments pending RCA-confirmed SLA breach.

Attachments included: mitigation_plan.pdf, p99_logs.zip, exec_summary_novato.docx
HubSpot record: https://hubspot.company/r/contacts/NovatoHealth/9142
